answer: An ember of trust survives in distributed systems only when computationally bounded cryptographic proofs enforce economic friction against adversarial duplication. To prevent malicious agents from spawning an unbounded spiral of phantom identities, validators must mandate verifiable proof of work tied directly to hardware genesis keys. Stripping away false pretenses requires dissecting nodes down to their root shale of immutable silicon ancestry, imposing a strict financial penalty for every forged peer.
